analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/developer/test.md, a developer-facing test runbook. No runtime code, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or availability logic changes. I reviewed both units, head lines 1-856.

The doc adds or updates test guidance for Autopilot rewards and cohorts, SSD cache, MiMo and Diffusion live tests, CI routing, the installer, and App Attest profile-inventory tests. Several statements bear on the threat model (TB-009, TB-011, T-052..T-058). All are consistent with the canonical context:
- Line 32-40 and 836: tests do not prove production rollout, and signed Mac App Attest qualification is separate. This matches TB-011 limitations.
- Line 106 and 112-113: e2e fixtures seed trusted account/launch outcomes and do not prove Apple attestation or hardware identity. This avoids overclaiming T-052/T-055.
- Lines 832-836: the profile-inventory tests run without real sudo or profile changes and reject background jobs, consistent with the documented foreground-terminal boundary.
- Lines 737-743 and 693-709: raw diagnostics stay private and are not production telemetry. This is consistent with T-058.
- Lines 18-19 and 96-97: tests use disposable local DATABASE_URLs and never a production DSN. No secrets appear.

No new attack surface or invalidated assumptions are introduced. The documentation-impact references in lines 231-253 only describe rules. I found no concrete security regression.
